Dallas County Data Questions and Responses (June 27, 2023):

Re-bucket youngest age categories to align with dept: youthful offenders 10-13 [holdoff on this until we talk to policy team]
Maybe look into the reasons for modifications prior to a technical violations. Are these modifications the result of a new offense? Discuss with policy team to decide if we should filter out extensions linked to new offense violations?
Combine unknown and not administered for risk and needs categories
Add mins and max to sections related to avg number of modification/extensions/technical violations/time to technical violation
Add row percentages to tables in technical violations descriptives section (section 2) of Who Receives Technical Violations page
Christian will follow up to confirm that using violation disposition of “DISMISSED OR WITHDRAWN BY DEPARTMENT” can always be interpreted as enrollment in 21-day CAI residential program
Follow up with Rhonda and Roger about what is included in “general violation” category and average length of supervision extensions.


Dallas County Data Questions and Responses (June 21, 2023):
We are curious to explore the proportion of violations filed by a PO that were then rejected by a supervisor. In our last conversation, you noted that all of the technical violation records without a referral number indicate that a PO filed the violation, but that it was rejected by a supervisor. In the violations data, we found that only about 2% of all violations fit this criteria. Does that seem correct to you all?

Lots of informal rejection is possible – will follow up with wordsmithing assistance. This reflects what is in the data system, but may not speak to the real trend.
POs will likely only formally file a violation if they feel confident.
PO has to get permission from supervisor before filing a violation so there should be very few rejected violations
TO DO:  Send file of rejected violations to Rhonda Kerl?


To look into technical violations leading to placement in the 30 day residential program (where if youth are successful, the violation is dismissed), we are using the violation disposition of “DISMISSED OR WITHDRAWN BY DEPARTMENT”. Just double checking, is this the correct violation disposition code to use? Is this disposition code only for youth who are successful in the program? If so, is there is a way to flag youth who are not successful?

Yes, this is successful. If youth did not successfully complete, we won’t see violation disposition, but instead should use placement file:
Placement == emergency shelter (on VOP)
Placement outcome == violation of court order
Completed == successful outcome; anything other than completed == not successful outcome
Also – CAI program is 21 days
TO DO:  Explore Christian’s strategy for flagging referral to CAI program that would capture both successful and unsuccessful completers. If things look right, use this flag instead and then re-run all pertinent analysis


Have there been any changes in the use of the 30 day residential program over time? Was it used less in 2020/2021 as a result of COVID? If so, have things changed back in more recent months?

CAI program (21 day program) – yes, things changed. Youth were served in detention center in more isolated settings (more 1-on-1 meetings, no group meetings). Hill center moved to more isolated programming, as well. Some youth were discharged on a quicker timetable than usual. 2-year period.


How should we interpret violations coded as new offenses in the violations file, but coded as VOPs in the offenses file? Were these new offenses that were never formally referred/filed and simply documented as VOPs?

VOP1 – not enough evidence or judge wants to keep youth on original felony charge (if new offense is just a low-level misdemeanor)
DA chose to file VOP as opposed to new offense. Example: If a kid is in on a felony but violated on a new offense that is lower level DA may choose to file VOP to keep felony as primary offense. If file new offense the lower offense would override the original felony. Kids have to have felony to be eligible for commitment.
TO DO:  Look into how often this happens. If often enough, we may not want to analyze new offenses by offense type (b/c we don’t have a representative sample). We’ll potentially need to exclude analysis.


We are hoping to calculate the average length of time that a supervision episode is extended as the result of a technical violation. If we just use the supervision extension file that you provided (and don’t join it with the violations file), is it a fairly safe assumption that the vast majority of supervision extensions we see are linked to a violation? Or are there other common non-violation reasons for supervision extensions?

Extension can be the result of agreed order, TV, or new offense.
Agreed order is usually used to extend for custody or to complete treatment/program or condition. Match extension file to violation file on dates.
Join on extension begin date and violation disposition date:
Within 3-5 days
Where violation disposition is modification? Can we use this? Do we have all dispositions for violations?
TO DO:  Change business rules to align with this new approach (-1 day or +3 days) and then re-run all pertinent analysis


We are currently exploring dispositions in the offenses file. Is it safe to assume that the most serious disposition is always linked to the most serious offense (i.e. DOI is “Primary”)? Or could the most serious disposition appear with the record of “Secondary” or “Dismissed” offense?

We already have first disposition for the referral – Christian already filtered on this. We don’t have any subsequent tacked on dispositions.


Dallas County Data Questions and Responses (April 2023):

In the supervision file there appears to be a small number of (around 170) supervision records that have duplicate referral IDs. They seem to have different start dates. How should we interpret these?
Response from Dallas: Transferring out of jurisdiction is a common reason. Deferred prosecution to failure to comply to pre-adjudication processing is another. Most duplicates should be turned into 1 record. Internal question: Should we drop deferred prosecution? VOP isn’t possible.
Do pure duplicates (every value is duplicated across all columns in files) in violations data file indicate multiple violations? Or should we de-duplicate this file? 
Response from Dallas: Christian will re-send file
Do missing supervision outcomes and supervision end dates indicate youth was under supervision at time of data pull? 
Response from Dallas: yes
For “Mental health needs status of the listed juvenile” in “Child” file – does that capture needs status at time of data pull/most recent assessment only? Or does it indicate if youth has ever had documented mental health needs? It appears that the substance use need variable indicates any history that youth have had with substance use services/needs. Is the same true for mental health needs? 
Response from Dallas: both are historic and reflect data at time of data pull
How should we interpret missing values for ‘prosecutor_action’, ‘prosecutor_action_date’, ‘disposition_date’, and ‘disposition’ in the violations file? Is there a reason these fields are missing for certain violation records (e.g., could missing disposition information indicate a VOP referral was dropped/withdrawn)?
Response from Dallas: Are used to access 30-day detention/programming, but not actually sent to prosecution (CIA is voluntary non-secure residential program used as sanction); if kid does well, violation won’t be sent on to prosecutor


“withdrawn” as disposition means department decision, not prosecutor
Blank disposition means referral is still pending
Missing referral number –PO filed violation, but supervisor rejected VOP (no action taken)
Prosecutor action fields are simply not complete – not sure we can use these fields for anything
Disposition is at referral-level – so most serious offense leads to dispo for entire referral including technicals

Christian added primary/secondary to indicate if specific offense/violation is leading to the listed dispo

What do a supervision phase of “None” and “Warrant” indicate? 
Response from Dallas:


Child has absconded and is on warrant during time period
None is deferred prosecution

Does supervision period start with disposition? Or can it include pre-disposition detention? Look at disposition dates and supervision start dates
Double check for any overlapping supervision periods by youth throughout file (create flag for this – I.e. multiple supervision records per youth with different referral IDs)

Calculate time between offense/violation date and disposition date – swift and certain punishment lens
Is this violation date or do we need to join back to offense file to get offense date/date of behavior
For technical only? Does this need to be a separate violation-level analytic file

Count of technical violation charges (unique violation records) per disposition (raw count)
Count of technical violation charges (unique violation records) per referral (raw count)

Create flag for prior supervision dispositions (based prior dispositions in offenses file)
Calculate length of time to first violation (both technical violation and new offense)
Group and de-dup violations file by disposition day and not referral ID (multiple referrals could be consolidated into a single disposition)
QUESTION: how we treat violations without dispositions/disposition dates? Should we group by disposition date, if present, and otherwise group by referral? Currently substituting violation file date for violations without disposition date. Need to confirm. From Emily: “Yes, I think we should group by disposition date only if present. So maybe we should keep in mind if we want to count violation type, we can look at offense or grouped by referral. If we want to know outcomes, we are only looking at those disposed.”

This syntax pulls in all data files provided by Dallas County stored as a series of Excel file tabs – and preliminarily maps their relationships with the datamodelr package (https://github.com/bergant/datamodelr)
File names reflect the names provided by Dallas County. Find more information on files and variables in Codebook tab.

Join 5. Join of supervision_child_join_offenses_5 and violations_clean_de_dup
Using a left join only joins offense records that led to supervision/disposition to supervision. Later, should I also join just by unique_id to capture offense records which occurred during supervision? The offense file is already de-duped by referral – keeping the most serious offense – so the file will still be unique by referral, supervision period, supervision extension, and supervision level
Logic to double check: only keeping violation records where the violation_date>=supervision_begin_date & violation_date<=supervision_end_date

  left_join(supervision_child_join_offenses_5,
            violations_clean_de_dup,
            by = c("unique_id")) %>% ### this is a many to many join so there are now lots of records (all violations joining to all supervisions/supervision extensions/supervision levels)
  ### now we need to filter on date -- only keeping violation records where the violation_date>=supervision_begin_date & violation_date<=supervision_end_date
  ### first create fake end date for records where the end date is blank; since this indicates that supervision was ongoing at time of data pull, we still want to include violations that occurred so changing NA to '2030-01-01' in new variable for the following filter
  mutate(supervision_end_date_missing_include = ifelse(is.na(supervision_end_date)==TRUE,
                                       ymd(as_date("2030-01-01")),
                                       ymd(as_date(supervision_end_date))),
         supervision_end_date_missing_include = ymd(as_date(supervision_end_date_missing_include)),
         ### flag records with no joining violation information using violation_referral_number
         no_violation_records_joined = ifelse(is.na(violation_referral_number==TRUE),
                                       1,0),
         ### flag records with joining violation information using dates
         violation_records_are_joined = ifelse(violation_date>=supervision_begin_date & violation_date<=supervision_end_date_missing_include,
                                       1,0),
         ### create date field for technical violations only
         ### we'll use this when keeping the first technical violation per referral
         technical_violation_filed_date = ifelse(violation_severity_factor=="Technical Violation",
                                                 violation_filed_date,
                                                 NA),
         technical_violation_filed_date = ymd(as_date(technical_violation_filed_date))) %>% 
        ### finally, create a flag for violation records that join 
        ### (i.e., youth has violation records), but
        ### do not have violations that fall within the given supervision period (for these records, we
        ### want to remove their violation data from the analytic file, 
        ### but ultimately keep all other data)
  mutate(has_violation_data_but_not_in_window_flag = ifelse(no_violation_records_joined==0 & (violation_date<supervision_begin_date | violation_date>supervision_end_date_missing_include),
                                                            1,0)) |> 
   ### recode all violation file values to NA if has_violation_data_but_not_in_window_flag==1
   ### this ensures that we do not accidentally use violation data for youth
   ### who only had violation that did not occur during the supervision periods in our sample (e.g., they had violations associated with supervision periods that occurred before the sample window)
  mutate(across(violation_referral_number:other_violation_count,
                ~ if_else(has_violation_data_but_not_in_window_flag==1,
                          NA, .))) %>%
  ### we only want to keep either (1) supervision records with no violations, (2) violation records that join (i.e., youth has violation records), but do not have violations that fall within the given supervision period, or (3) supervision records with violation records when those violations occurred during the period of supervision  
  filter(no_violation_records_joined==1 | has_violation_data_but_not_in_window_flag==1 | (violation_date>=supervision_begin_date & violation_date<=supervision_end_date_missing_include)) %>% 
  group_by(unique_supervision_id) %>% 
  ### now create these flags at the supervision episode level
  ### so that we can drop records from supervision episodes with joined violation records that fit criteria #2 above (e.g., youth has both historic and current violation records that joined. because we won't entirely drop the youth/supervision episode if we remove the historic records, we should drop the historic records and only keep violations which occurred during pertinent supervision episode)
  mutate(no_violation_records_joined_supervision_level = max(no_violation_records_joined),
         has_violation_data_but_not_in_window_flag_supervision_level = max(has_violation_data_but_not_in_window_flag),
         violation_records_are_joined_supervision_level = max(violation_records_are_joined)) |> 
  ungroup() |> 
  
#################################################
### Code review w/ Becky left off here
################################################

  ### now create flag and filter on it -- based on above logic/rationale
  mutate(has_joined_violation_data_drop_record = ifelse(violation_records_are_joined_supervision_level==1 & has_violation_data_but_not_in_window_flag==1,
                                                        1,0)) |> 
  filter(has_joined_violation_data_drop_record==0) |> 
  group_by(unique_supervision_id) %>% 
  ### count of referrals linked to any violation (using no_violation_records_joined), technical violations, and new offense violations
  mutate(overall_violation_referral_count = n_distinct(violation_referral_number[no_violation_records_joined==0],
                                                         na.rm = TRUE),
         technical_violation_referral_count = n_distinct(violation_referral_number[no_violation_records_joined==0 & violation_severity_factor=="Technical Violation"],
                                                         na.rm = TRUE),
         new_offense_violation_referral_count = n_distinct(violation_referral_number[no_violation_records_joined==0 & violation_severity_factor=="New Offense"],
                                                           na.rm = TRUE),
         min_technical_violation_date = min(technical_violation_filed_date,
                                            na.rm = TRUE)) %>% 
  ungroup() %>% 
  ### now de-dup by supervision record to get same row count as before join 
  ### first arrange by unique_supervision_id and violation date to keep first
  ### violation date
  arrange(unique_supervision_id,
          violation_filed_date) |> 
  distinct(unique_supervision_id,
           .keep_all=TRUE) %>% 
  ### calculate time to first technical violation (with both vars)
  mutate(supervision_start_first_tech_violation_any = as.numeric(difftime(min_technical_violation_date,
                                                            supervision_begin_date,
                                                                    units="days")),
         supervision_start_first_tech_violation_first_overall = as.numeric(difftime(violation_filed_date,
                                                            supervision_begin_date,
                                                                    units="days"))) |> 
  mutate(technical_violation_flag = ifelse(technical_violation_referral_count>0 & !is.na(overall_violation_referral_count)==TRUE,
                                           1,0),
         overall_violation_referral_flag = ifelse(overall_violation_referral_count>0 & !is.na(overall_violation_referral_count)==TRUE,
                                                  1,0))

                                       ymd(as_date("2030-01-01")),
                                       ymd(as_date(supervision_end_date))),
         violation_date = ymd(as_date(violation_date)),
         ### create var with day subtracted for modification date logic (as extra buffer)
         ### business rule: modification phase date must be less than violation date -1 day
         violation_date_plus_one_day = violation_date - lubridate::days(1),
         violation_date_missing_include = ifelse(is.na(violation_date)==TRUE,
                                       ymd(as_date("2030-01-01")),
                                       ymd(as_date(violation_date))),
         supervision_end_date_missing_include = ymd(as_date(supervision_end_date_missing_include)),
         ### flag records with no joining modification information using supervision_level_phase_begin_date
         no_modification_records_joined = ifelse(is.na(supervision_level_phase_begin_date==TRUE),
                                       1,0)) %>% 
  ### we only want to keep either (1) violation records with no modifications or (2) supervision records with violation records when those violations occurred during the period of supervision  
  ### we only want records that fit our criteria of:
  ### violations occurring during the supervision episode
  ### so we are dropping violations here that occurred outside sample window for supervision episodes (FY 2018 through FY 2023)
  filter(no_modification_records_joined==1 | (violation_date>=supervision_begin_date & violation_date<=supervision_end_date_missing_include)) %>% 
  ### only technical violations
  ### and only modifications which mark an increase in intensiveness
  filter(violation_severity_factor=="Technical Violation",
          supervision_level_is_increase_flag==1) %>% 
  ### for this analysis, keep first violation per supervision episode 
  ### de-dup, keeping first record to preserve violation and linked modifications for supervision period
  ### also keep earliest supervision_level_phase_begin_date that joined
  arrange(unique_supervision_id,
          violation_date,
          supervision_level_phase_begin_date) %>%
  distinct(unique_supervision_id,
           .keep_all = TRUE) %>% 
  ### and modifications occurring before the violation
  ### and only modifications that were increases in intensiveness
  ### when we de-dup, we will keep first violation per supervision episode
  filter(no_modification_records_joined==1 | (supervision_level_phase_begin_date<violation_date_plus_one_day)) %>% 
  dplyr::select(unique_id,
                violation_referral_number,
                referral_number,
                unique_supervision_id,
                violation,
                violation_date,
                violation_date_plus_one_day,
                supervision_begin_date,
                supervision_end_date,
                supervision_end_date_missing_include,
                supervision_level_phase,
                supervision_level_phase_begin_date,
                supervision_level_phase_end_date,
                supervision_level_is_increase_flag) %>% 
  distinct() %>% 
  mutate(unique_modification_id = paste0(unique_supervision_id,
                                         supervision_level_phase_begin_date,
                                         supervision_level_phase_end_date)) |> 
  ### anti-join modification_prior_to_technical_violation_count and supervision_modification_new_offense_violations_only 
  ### keeping only modification records which appear in modification_prior_to_technical_violation_count BUT not in supervision_modification_new_offense_violations_only
  anti_join(supervision_modification_new_offense_violations_only,
            by = "unique_modification_id") |> 
  group_by(unique_supervision_id,
          violation_date) %>%
  ### at this point, we only have records that fit our criteria of 
  ### technical violations occurring during the supervision episode
  ### modifications occurring before the violation
  ### and only modifications that were increases in intensiveness
  ### when we de-dup, we will keep first violation per supervision episode
  ### now count modifications per violations
  mutate(modification_increase_prior_to_technical_count = n_distinct(unique_id,
                                                  unique_supervision_id,
                                                  supervision_level_phase,
                                                  supervision_level_phase_begin_date)) %>% 
  ungroup() %>% 
 
  dplyr::select(unique_supervision_id,
                modification_increase_prior_to_technical_count)
